posts.title: Collaborative Software Development in the Age of AI
posts.description: Lately, a question keeps coming up: Is Free and Open Source Software (FOSS) becoming obsolete in the golden age of AI? If AI can rewrite anything from scratch, hasn’t FOSS lost its purpose? If you reduce FOSS to the provisioning of source code, then perhaps. But FOSS was never just about the code itself - and AI doesn’t change that. In fact, its core principles may become even more vital. The Esse

posts.title: If AI can rewrite anything: What's left of copyright and copyleft?
posts.description: Every software license - from a proprietary EULA to the GNU GPL - rests on a single convention: that computer code is copyrightable, and that copying its expression is something different from reimplementing its ideas. posts.title: Corporate Responsibility: Open Source isn’t a side project — It’s your product
posts.description: Companies are undoubtedly enormously benefiting from Free and Open Source Software (FOSS). To bring innovative and profitable products to market, they draw extensively on the amazing work of the global FOSS community.
